stem: In her school science class in Jaipur, Meera observes an Amoeba under the microscope and also looks at a diagram of a human body. Her teacher asks: which of the following statements about living organisms is correct? () A. Only large plants and animals are made of cells; tiny organisms like bacteria are not made of cells; B. An organism made of only one cell cannot be considered a complete living organism; C. All living organisms are made of cells; a single cell can form a complete organism, and many cells together can form a larger organism; D. Only organisms visible to the naked eye are made of cells

options.text: Only large plants and animals are made of cells; tiny organisms like bacteria are not made of cells
An organism made of only one cell cannot be considered a complete living organism
All living organisms are made of cells; a single cell can form a complete organism, and many cells together can form a larger organism
Only organisms visible to the naked eye are made of cells

teacher.key_rationale: C states the correct rule: all living beings are made of cells, and a cell is the basic unit of life — one cell can be a whole unicellular organism (e.g., Amoeba, bacteria), and many cells build a multicellular organism (e.g., human). A wrongly excludes microbes; B wrongly denies that a unicellular organism is complete; D wrongly ties cell-based structure to visibility.
